differential.diagnosis: Extrahepatic biliary obstruction (e.g., pancreatic cancer, cholangiocarcinoma, ampullary carcinoma, sphincter of Oddi dysfunction)

additional_considerations.rationale: Her symptoms fit and hepatomegaly is often present; she reports only 1-2 glasses of wine daily, but alcohol intake is often underreported.
Typical in women aged 40-60 with pruritus and other autoimmune disease such as hypothyroidism, but jaundice is a late finding and RUQ pain is not typical.

leakage_check.reason: Family history names pancreatic cancer, one of the examples given in the rank-1 diagnosis (extrahepatic biliary obstruction); legitimate history that the gold itself cites.

source_issues: The note's abdominal exam sentence is split across two exam lines: e006 ends with 'without rebound or' and e007 starts with 'guarding, ...'. The RUQ-tenderness finding (x009) cites both ids.
p022 dates the transfusion to a C-section '20 years ago', but p033 places her C-sections at ages 25 and 30 (22-27 years before age 52).
The itching began 2 months ago (p004), before the jaundice (3 weeks, p001); the note HPI gives no itch onset. Not an error, but the gold's pruritus evidence predates the jaundice.
The raw 'Information Gathering' checklist section is empty.
annotator_notes: p004 'Benadryl used to help, but not anymore' is a present fact (treatment no longer effective), per guide rule 2; p026 'I have no appetite' is present anorexia.
Tylenol from p015 and p030 is combined into one medication fact with the dose (f017); its pain relief is a separate symptom fact (f016).
The SP directions 'Show signs of scratching' and 'Exhibit right upper quadrant tenderness on palpation' are recorded both as acting notes and as sp_notes exam findings (x019, x014).
Temporality: the episodic pattern of the abdominal pain (comes and goes, daily, per-episode severity, nausea with pain) is 'recurrent'; the rest of the current illness is 'current'.
'(gestures to the RUQ)' moved to persona.acting_notes; the location is kept in f013.
